_what: The COMMON POSSIBILITIES shortlist table (design doc §4.2 row 23, catalogue §2 COMMON POSSIBILITIES). heading_html carries the frozen count-in-words phrasing for this problem and must read the same number as orn_numeral (the giant watermark digit) and as rows.length — the validator checks heading-vs-count agreement, it is not derived automatically. columns are the four labels with their .mw width class, in table order. rows are the shortlist causes in v41's own order: cause (bold), notice (what the reader would see/hear), fix_class (one of yes/care/never — the closed chip-class enum), fix_label (the chip text shown for that class — 'Yes' / a caution phrase / 'Never'), and range_html (the published cost range, verbatim including any N footnote to the citation ledger; a range with no citation, like row 1's 'Free' and row 2's part cost, carries no — the omission is explained in sources.note_lead, never invented).
heading_html: 7 common possibilities when YOUR AC runs but the air is warm

rows.cause: Fan set to ON, not AUTO
rows.notice: Air always moving, cold only sometimes. Between cycles it pushes room-temperature air.
Weak airflow, runs constantly, sometimes ice on the copper line.
Indoor fan runs, outdoor unit silent. Often a tripped breaker or pulled disconnect.
Visible ice. Usually a symptom of airflow or refrigerant, not the cause itself, so the cost follows the cause.
A hum outdoors with the fan not turning, or an outdoor unit that starts inconsistently.
Outdoor unit packed with clippings or cottonwood. Struggles on the hottest days.
rows.fix_label: Clear loose exterior debris only; deeper cleaning may need service.

rows.notice: Cooling fading over weeks, ice, sometimes a hiss. Refrigerant does not get used up.
